newsitem.title: USA: Applied Extrusion sees strong sales, revs.
newsitem.headline: Applied Extrusion sees strong sales, revs.

text.p: Applied Extrusion Technologies Inc on Tuesday reported that fiscal first quarter ended December 31 sales rose 18 percent from a year ago and forecast strong quarterly increases in sales and profitability for the rest of the year.
The company earlier reported quarterly sales of $59.4 million, up from the $50.3 million reported a year ago. Gross profit of $13.5 million was up 19 percent from a year ago.

The company cited the initial impact of the new capacity brought on-stream in fiscal 1996. It said investments made in new product development and an expanded sales force to support the 30 percent increase in capacity resulted in a higher level of related selling, research and administrative expenditures.

"This increased level of operating expenditures will not only support the significant volume growth for the balance of fiscal 1997, but more importantly, with nominal increases will support the additional 25 percent increase in capacity scheduled to commence in the second quarter of fiscal 1998," it said.

"We are pleased with the continuing improvement in the OPP films industry, and our success in achieving record sales levels and production volumes," said Thomas Williams, president and chief executive officer.

"We believe our most challenging quarter related to financial performance is now behind us, and we expect strong quarterly increases in sales and profitability for the balance of the year. The factors negatively impacting margins in the first quarter, namely high resin costs and the lack of price increases coming into the year, both appear to be improving," he added.
